text:
harry: Quick follow-up from today's RFC workshop — we sketched the idea of a tiny set of "intent" claims on API keys (read/write/ingest/admin) + an optional "actor" claim for service-to-service flows. Wanted to capture open tradeoffs before I file the follow-up RFC.

olivia: +1 for documenting tradeoffs. main worry: how do we map intent -> effective RBAC? we still need per-resource checks in many places.

sara: agree. also think we should be explicit about validity lifetimes. short-lived vs long-lived keys change how much we can trust intent-only keys.

mike: quick notes from infra perspective: routing + telemetry rely heavily on a single canonical identity field today (project_id). If we add actor vs intent, runtime needs to preserve both on every request, or we'll break existing metrics and quota.

harry: good point. proposal: token surface adds two lightweight attrs: intent and actor (both optional). runtime keeps project_id and attaches these to request envelope. Default behavior when absent: intent="unknown", actor="service". Thoughts?

jenn: i like the minimality. but how do we prevent principals from granting themselves escalated intents? e.g., a customer creating api-key with intent=admin.

olivia: ops guardrails: only org-admins can mint admin-intent keys. otherwise keys default to least privileged intent. we should enforce at mint time + have runtime assert that admin-intent tokens are only used by allowed callers.

sara: we also discussed later about mapping to roles. maybe intent is a coarse-grain attribute for routing and cheap checks, and we still do full RBAC checks at enforcement points. intent can short-circuit expensive checks for low-risk routes.

mike: from runtime perf POV that makes sense. intent short-circuit for allow-once-per-seconds counters, but any state-changing write or billing API must call the RBAC service.

harry: agreed. action items I'm thinking: 1) add mint-time policy for intents 2) add runtime envelope fields 3) update metrics to record intent+actor 4) define a compact assertion format for cross-region handoffs. Any missing?

jenn: add audit log content: record the minting principal + allowed intents + mint policy id. we need to be able to answer "who could've created this key" for incidents.

olivia: question about the "actor" claim: do we expect actor to be an opaque service-id or a human actor email? mixing them is confusing.

sara: we should define actor_type enum (service|human|operator) and actor_id string. keep both small. example:

```
actor_type: "service"
actor_id: "billing-pipeline:v2"
```

mike: runtime change: we need to add those fields to the request envelope protobuf. simple patch, but lots of services read raw headers, not envelope. rollout plan required.

harry: rollout idea: 1) mint-time + logs only (no enforcement) for 2 weeks 2) metrics + telemetry consumers updated 3) runtime asserts added in a canary env 4) enforcement rollout with knob to treat missing actor as "unknown" 5) full enforcement minimum 2 weeks later

jenn: thumbs-up. also propose a safe fallback for older clients: if no intent claim, treat as intent=limited and require additional auth for sensitive endpoints.

olivia: one more tradeoff: if intent is mutable (i.e., can be edited) we get easier ops but more complex revocation. prefer immutability with short TTLs + rotation.

harry: immutability + rotation seems reasonable. we'll allow creating new keys with different intent but old ones remain valid until TTL. include rotation helpers in the console.

sara: can we add a small lint step in minting API to warn if intent doesn't match requested scopes? e.g., api-key labeled "ingest" but scope includes write:billing.

mike: totally. lint + enforcement is great. console and SDKs can surface warnings.

dev-bot: deploy-checklist: add schema for token claims to proto repo, update mint service, add telemetry hook, update docs. /cc @infra @console

harry: ok i'll draft the follow-up RFC with these sections: goals, claim schema (intent + actor_type + actor_id), mint-time policy, runtime envelope changes, rollout plan, metrics/audit additions, examples, migration plan. I'll assign owners for each.

olivia: thanks. please call out the explicit policy that only org-admins can mint admin intent keys and that all admin-intent uses require RBAC guardrail at enforcement.

jenn: and add a paragraph on incident response: how to revoke keys quickly and how telemetry surfaces unusual intent usage patterns.

harry: will do. if no objections i'll push a first draft by EOD and ping this thread for review. :thumbsup:

sara: no objections from me.

mike: +1

jenn: +1
